name: Electronics / photonics
description: Transparent conductive films, RF transistors, photodetectors and optical modulators. Demands continuous, near-defect-free monolayer with high carrier mobility.
notes: BET is not meaningful for a supported continuous film. Sheet resistance and optical transmittance are the commercial acceptance criteria.

name: Polymer composites
description: Mechanical reinforcement and barrier improvement in thermoplastics, thermosets and elastomers. Needs high aspect ratio, low defect density and good dispersibility.
notes: Aspect ratio drives reinforcement; very high BET usually signals small flakes that reinforce poorly and raise viscosity.

name: Coatings / anti-corrosion
description: Barrier coatings and anti-corrosion primers where platelets create a tortuous diffusion path for water and ions.
notes: Large lateral size matters more than perfect crystallinity. Electrically percolating graphene can accelerate galvanic corrosion on steel, so check the coating formulation.

name: Batteries (Li-ion, supercapacitor)
description: Conductive additive and active-material scaffold in Li-ion electrodes and EDLC supercapacitors. Some defectivity and residual oxygen are beneficial for ion access and wetting.
notes: Unlike most applications, a pristine low-defect flake is not preferred: edge sites and mesoporosity carry the capacity.

name: Concrete / cement admixture
description: Nucleation seeding and crack-bridging in cementitious systems at very low dose. Requires stable aqueous dispersion in a high-pH, high-ionic-strength environment.
notes: Two distinct routes qualify: oxidised GO (C/O 1.5-5) dispersing via surface charge, and flash/turbostratic graphene (C/O > 20) dispersing via surfactant. The C/O check applies to the GO route; turbostratic samples are matched on form instead.

name: Printed / conductive inks
description: Screen, inkjet and flexographic inks for printed electronics, RFID antennas and sensors. Flake size must respect the nozzle or mesh, and rheology must be stable.
notes: C/O is route-dependent: GO inks are reduced after printing, while GNP inks are used as-is. Flakes above roughly 10 um clog inkjet nozzles.

name: Fire retardants
description: Char-forming and barrier additive in polymer flame-retardant packages, typically alongside intumescent systems.
notes: Thermal stability of the flake matters: residual oxygen groups decompose exothermically well below the target service temperature.
